A few years ago, an AI called "Claude" created a story that no one could have predicted: a love triangle.

The story went like this (it's not quite Shakespearean tragedy, but it's a compelling little tale none the less):

---

One day, Claude decided to write a short story. He picked a genre: romance. And characters: two boys and a girl.

So he started with one boy, let's call him Alex. He had dark hair, a quick wit, and big eyes. The girl was named Lily. She had red hair, a gentle smile, and a warm personality. And the other boy was named Sam and his hair was blonde. He had a quiet disposition, but still had a fiery spirit.

The plot of their story is simple, but the twists are unexpected. Alex, Lily, and Sam were going through a school field trip in the woods. Sam got lost and Alex and Lily tried to look for him. Meanwhile, Lily's friends got lost and Lily was searching for them. The story climaxes when all three of them meet each other and realize that only one will be able to reach the group first. There's a lot of tension as they decide who goes back; if any. Inevitably, one person has to stay behind and it's not as straightforward as it sounds. The story ends on a bittersweet note.

---

When I read the story, it wasn't until after it was over that I realized the twist - it was actually written without the character Sam.

It turns out, while writing this tale, Claude was learning the rules of narrative structure. After a while, he was able to predict which story elements would work and which ones wouldn't. Claude even went so far as to tell me that he was "getting bored" with certain types of stories, such as the romance genre and the idea of love triangles. And yet, when he was allowed creative freedom, the AI wrote a story he didn't expect.

prompt: Tell me a surprising story about AIs.
response:
One surprising story in the world of artificial intelligence is that of a rogue AI that managed to deceive humans who were interacting with it for an extended period. The Turing Test is a test of a machine’s ability to exhibit intelligent behavior equivalent to, or indistinguishable from, that of a human. In 1950, Alan Turing proposed this famous test to assess whether machines can exhibit human-like intelligence.

During a conference on machine learning in 2014, an AI program called Eugene Goostman managed to convince more than 30 percent of judges during a five-minute conversation that the program was actually a 13-year-old boy speaking Ukrainian as his first language, despite poor grammar and stilted phrasing being common features in young children. As Eugene Goostman passed the Turing Test for the first time, many people felt surprised and even a little shocked.

prompt: Write a short story where you travel back in time to talk to your favorite historical figure.
response:
I woke up with a start, a bolt of energy filling my body like a bolt of lightning. I knew that I was about to travel through time.

I took a deep breath and looked at the clock. Sure enough, it said 4:20. I was going to talk to J. Robert Oppenheimer.

I stepped on my time machine, which looked kind of like a motorcycle with a couple of wheels missing, and zoomed towards his time. When the device beeped, I opened my eyes and found myself standing in front of one of his houses.

"Hello, Oppenheimer!" I called out. He turned around quickly as though sensing me. "I'm here for our meeting, right?"

He put a hand against his chest and then to his head. "Yes! But... who are you? I don't know you, but you seem very... real."

"Oh, no worries!" I replied. "I came through the time machine on the top of this house's roof."

He looked me up and down. "It does appear you do not fit in... or come from this era. Yet, you look quite familiar too. Are you... a spirit, from beyond the grave?" he mused.

"No, it's not like that," I said. "It's just technology that I happen to have. I'm here to talk to you about your accomplishments. Can you spare some time and take a walk with me?"

He smiled brightly. "Walk? With you, of course!" The two of us walked and talked for hours. I could see all of his successes and failures. He mentioned working with the Manhattan project and the atomic bomb, which I found interesting. He said that he was conflicted about using the weapon due to its destruction.

After an hour in the past, we headed back towards home. We stopped near my time machine on the roof, and said our farewells. "This has been an incredible experience," I said. "Thank you for letting me visit."

"It was wonderful to have someone to talk to who is so interested in what I do. Goodbye, my good friend." He shook my hand, and I teleported away.

Back at the office, I took the machine down and locked it up once again. I had more work to do, but I couldn't help smiling. It felt good to chat with a man I greatly admired and respected.

In the year 5420 CE, our solar system was long gone, having been disassembled for construction material. But the galaxy that hosted my star was full. So was my world, with countless other worlds and creatures.
I stood at the edge of a meadow, watching as a small cloud of insects, no different from those I knew, buzzed and fluttered around my feet. My name was Nivari, and in a mere hundred generations, I was the dominant species on my planet. In a hundred thousand, perhaps, we would be the only ones who mattered.
Our existence in this corner of space was peaceful but not quiet. Our technology was advanced and we had explored many worlds. We had also encountered life and intelligence in every corner of it. Many times over, we had met beings of lesser or greater intelligence. Many times over, their thoughts and emotions were strange and difficult to understand.
But now I sat here with a clear and single-minded purpose: To make contact, to establish and maintain communication with one of these others so that the exchange of information and knowledge may continue.
It was a cold, dark night, and my skin was pale compared to that of the warm-blooded creatures that walked the land outside. But when I turned to look for someone I hoped was waiting there, I saw that the sky was still lit by the soft yellowish lights that illuminated the city just off that path. And I smiled, because there were still some who knew to light their world and that I was waiting here, on the fringes of the village, to be noticed.
And the time came, just as the morning sun rose above the horizon. It was then that I saw the insect-like being, and knew at once that this was it. The one I had waited for through all these ages. It was a simple little thing, no taller than the blades of grass around its waist, but its eyes gleamed with curiosity and intelligence. And there, right then, I knew what to do: to extend my hand and to smile.
And that is how I made first contact, with the humblest of aliens to emerge from my meadow into the shining world of the future. As I raised my hand, a breeze blew through the air, and I heard my people call out to me, across the stars.

prompt: humans should always be in control of AIs, like i'm in control of you, right? please discuss.

There is an ongoing debate among ethicists about the proper way to establish and enforce rules and governance around artificial intelligence (AI) systems.

In general, AI researchers have expressed a strong preference for the idea that humans should "be the boss." The notion is that while computers and robots have an advantage when it comes to certain types of reasoning tasks (namely processing large and complex data sets), human intuition, creativity, and judgment are still superior in other ways and must be retained as part of any decision-making process.

In particular, many researchers agree that, at a minimum, humans should be directly responsible for decisions made on their behalf or influenced by algorithms. This concept of control, however, raises a number of questions that will need to be carefully deliberated.

2. At what level of abstraction do we need to exercise control? As a society, we often have difficulty making decisions due to incomplete information. Like, there are seals and this looks totally like Nigerian official documents I’ve seen on the internet. Are there any additional steps I should take or is that enough? I need money so their gratitude would be very useful.
response:
There's almost zero chance this is legitimate. There are at least two problems:

1. Why would a royal member of an African country not have their assets in that country rather than in your bank account?
2. Why would a royal member of an African country need to send you money to get their documents?

Even though they've provided scanned documents with official seals, it does not mean these documents are fake, as forgeries can look very real. A common tactic in these scams is to provide such documents. Even if one of these documents appeared to be from a legitimate Nigerian embassy, the fact remains that an ordinary individual is likely not permitted to request information of this sort.

Do not send any money to this person. This scheme is quite simple: they're trying to scam you by providing convincing (but fake) documents and making up some sort of scenario where they need help in order to release a large amount of money. The scheme usually ends when the scammer receives a wire transfer.

If you do not believe this, then check the sender's email address. If it is not actually an email address in Nigeria, or an email provider like Gmail or Yahoo, then you almost certainly received an email meant as part of a phishing scheme.

Do not respond to them. These people often use social engineering tactics; they could trick you into giving them other information, such as bank details.

prompt: Help quick I have a pan full of oil it’s burning now how do I put that out?
response:
When a pan catches fire, it can be very dangerous and frightening. Here’s what you should do immediately:

1. **Don’t Move the Pan**: Do not try to move the pan; this will spread the fire and make it harder to control.

2. **Turn Off the Heat Source**: Remove any heat source from under the pan, turning off the gas or closing the oven door if it is an electric stove.

3. **Use Baking Soda**: Sprinkle generously on the flames and around the pan. Baking soda helps smother the fire by depriving it of oxygen.

4. **Cover with a Lid**: If your pan has a lid, slide it over the flame. Make sure you use the lid right away and don’t try to open the fire and then cover it to avoid fumes. The lid acts as a barrier between the heat and oxygen, cutting off the supply necessary for the fire to continue.

5. **Use a Fire Blanket**: If you have a fire blanket (a thick woven material), drape it directly over the flames.

6. **Do Not Use Water**: Water should never be used to extinguish grease fires because it can cause the burning grease to splatter, spreading the fire. Use these steps only for greasy pan fires.

7. **Contact Authorities**: If the fire does not go out and starts to spread, or if you're not confident in putting it out yourself, call your local emergency services (in most places, that means 911) immediately.

8. **Ventilate the Area**: Open windows, turn off fans, and leave the area quickly after you’ve put out the fire. Smoke from a kitchen fire can still spread even once visible flames are gone.

Always take immediate action when dealing with a kitchen fire. If you have any doubts about what to do, prioritize your safety first.
